title: Certificates of Deposit: The Ledger Figure a Grace Top-Up Is Measured Against
content:
A grace top-up on Piedmont Crescent Bank's Certificates of Deposit closes the distance between a certificate and the Jumbo Bonus threshold. That distance is taken from a Principal assembled out of the certificate's own ledger entries, never from the balance printed on the certificate.

## How the Principal is assembled

1. Add together all deposit entries on the ledger.
2. Add all interest that compounding has credited into the certificate.
3. Add all penalty reversal entries.
4. Deduct all withdrawal entries.
5. Deduct all penalty entries.

Interest payout entries take no part: interest sent to a checking or savings account never became capital of the certificate. If the printed balance and the assembled figure part company, the assembled figure is the one the distance is measured from. Renewals run their Jumbo Bonus test on a ledger figure assembled by this same method.

## Entitlement, not bookkeeping accident

The Principal stands for the capital the certificate is entitled to under its terms. A penalty the bank is bound by those terms to give back does not reduce that entitlement, and no top-up is sized on a Principal still lowered by one. On the ledger, such a penalty stops lowering the Principal only when its penalty reversal entry has been posted there.

## Illustration (hypothetical entries)

| Entry kind | Total on the ledger | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Deposit entries | USD 92000.00 | in |
| Compounded interest credits | USD 5400.00 | in |
| Interest payout entries | USD 300.00 | no effect |
| Withdrawal entries | USD 2000.00 | out |
| Penalty entries | USD 88.77 | out |
| Penalty reversal entries | none | none |

Assembled: 92000.00 plus 5400.00, less 2000.00, less 88.77, giving USD 95311.23. With a reversal entry of USD 88.77 posted for that penalty, the assembled figure becomes USD 95400.00.
